function: Distributed downlink precoding in cell-free massive MIMO; excluded no_learning: over-the-air Riemannian gradient descent of the precoders, a model-based iterative algorithm (p. 1, p. 4, p. 5, p. 10).
notes: Excluded, no_learning. The 'quasi-NN' is an analogy: the AP precoders (and MMSE UE combiners) are treated as network weights and optimized directly for the current channel by over-the-air gradient descent, p. 4: "We adopt the first-order Riemannian gradient descent method [26] to optimize"; p. 5 (Algorithm 1): "T rounds of DL-UL ping-pong iterations conducted over-the-air". No model is trained on data and reused: p. 1: "it differs from an ANN as it is model-based and optimized in real time"; p. 10: "a model-based approach and is fully-interpretable". Backpropagation is only the inspiration (abstract, p. 1); results average 100 Monte Carlo channel realizations and UE drops (p. 9), and the system "needs to be retrained periodically" as the channel varies (p. 8), i.e. re-optimization. Codes 1-2 do not apply (research article, not a survey). Had it been judged learned, it would be area 3 (multi-antenna APs and UEs, no RIS, p. 8). Title and DOI confirmed on p. 1.
